title: Follow the Leader: Enhancing Systematic Trend-Following Using Network Momentum

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper constructs a systematic trend-following strategy that combines univariate time-series momentum with network momentum derived from cross-sectional momentum spillover. Lead-lag relationships between asset pairs are detected using signature-based Lévy area and various dynamic time warping (DTW, DDTW, shapeDTW) algorithms. A convex graph learning optimization problem is then solved to convert the pairwise lead-lag matrices into a sparse, normalized network momentum adjacency matrix. Portfolios are formed using moving-average crossover signals weighted by this adjacency matrix, scaled to target volatility, and tested using stationary block-bootstrapped data and real historical commodity and index futures prices.
extraction.universe: 28 futures markets spanning agriculture, energy, metals, and equity indices

key_findings: Combining univariate time-series momentum with network momentum derived from lead-lag relationships significantly improves net Sharpe ratios and Sortino ratios over the baseline MACD model.
Network momentum models consistently produce more positively skewed returns, indicating superior management of downside risk while capturing large gains.
Ensemble methods utilizing multiple lookback windows reduce transaction costs and lower strategy turnover compared to single-window network momentum models.
Network momentum models significantly outperform the benchmark in short trading positions, where univariate trend-following models typically incur losses.
limitations: The tested portfolio market selection is somewhat random and performance may not be fully reproducible for other specific sets of assets.
P&L is calculated using estimated historical transaction costs based on half the average bid-ask spread.
